name: Nancy Mace
role: U.S. Representative from South Carolina (2021-2027); 2026 Republican candidate for governor
summary: Mace is a Republican who started as a fiscal conservative and conservation-minded legislator and has moved steadily toward Trump-aligned positions on immigration, gender and crime. She supports school choice, term limits, a balanced budget amendment and the Second Amendment, favours the death penalty, and is pro-life with exceptions for rape, incest and the mother's life. She has also backed animal welfare and cannabis reform and voted against the April 2024 Ukraine aid package and FISA renewal.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Her healthcare page says the free market delivers better quality at lower prices and that the federal government must loosen its grip on healthcare decisions; in 2013-2020 she called for full repeal of ObamaCare.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: States on her healthcare page that the free market delivers a higher-quality product at a lower price, and in the 2026 debate said "I'm a free market girl. I love competition."

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Her spending page rejects the argument that Americans are not paying their "fair share", calling taking more money by force no solution; her platform is to cut taxes, including eliminating the state income tax.

property-fundamental.rationale: Opposing civil asset forfeiture is nearby; no stated general position on property rights.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mixed record: she introduced a bill to block regulations that raise household costs, but also pushes pesticide limits and data-centre cost rules on companies.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted No on FISA reauthorization in April 2024, saying she could not support the government spying on Americans while accepting a balance with security.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Cannabis descheduling is nearby; no stated position on legalizing recreational drugs generally.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Her No Funds for Fascists Act objects to the UK and Germany jailing people for "offensive" tweets, calling it Orwellian madness.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted against the assault weapons ban, saying "gun control and gun bans don't work" and she is a gun owner and hunter; favours better background-check data instead.

empower-police-military.rationale: Votes against bills to "defund the police" and secures defence authorisation provisions; also backs police-accountability measures such as limits on union protection of bad officers.

decide-locally.rationale: States on her Constitution page that each state has the right to govern itself free from excessive federal intrusion, and welcomed Dobbs for returning power to states.

rehabilitation.rationale: Her civil rights page says everyone has the potential for rehabilitation and opposes spending on incarcerating non-violent offenders, while she supports capital punishment for the worst crimes.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Said in 2022 she always supports the right of any two people to marry and voted for the Respect for Marriage Act; contested because from 2025 she made sharply critical statements about gay couples and books without retracting.

abortion-legal.rationale: States she is pro-life with exceptions for rape, incest and the life of the mother, the same position as President Trump; accepts gestational limits of 15-20 weeks.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Her TRANS Government Research Act release says sex is binary, "not a spectrum" and "not a social construct".

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Her No Immigration Without Assimilation Act says America has every right to protect its culture, laws and people.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Introduced bills to ban immigration from dozens of countries, from Somalia, Sudan and South Sudan, and to end birthright citizenship for children of illegal immigrants.

free-trade.rationale: Her trade page calls keeping trade "free, fair, and open with as many countries as possible" her top priority.

nation-first.rationale: Repeatedly frames policy as "America First", saying she will not put foreign interests ahead of American citizens.

open-borders.rationale: Her issue page calls illegal immigration a crisis requiring decisive action; she sponsored bills to expand expedited removal and ban entry from listed countries.

expand-nuclear.rationale: In the 2026 debate listed small nuclear reactors among the options to meet South Carolina's energy crisis.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Her trade page warns that taxing imported products risks jobs and raises prices for Lowcountry families.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Her bill treats belief in religious law replacing or operating parallel to U.S. law as incompatible with American principles.

military-superiority.rationale: Wrote "We should have the strongest national defense in the world. Period." and praises "peace through strength".

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Co-led the ENCRYPT Act, objecting to law-enforcement pressure on firms to weaken security with backdoors.

school-vouchers.rationale: Introduced the School Freedom Act (Oct 2026) to let federal education money follow each child to any public, private, charter or home school; platform backs universal school choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Voted against the American Rescue Plan and says deficit spending feeds inflation; backs the "Penny Plan" to balance the budget.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Introduced the Preserving Social Security and Medicare for Citizens Act limiting benefits to citizens, nationals and lawful permanent residents.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Describes race-based caucuses as segregation sanctioned by the legislature and objects to sorting people by race.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: No Immigration Without Assimilation Act denies entry to people who refuse to assimilate into American culture.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Her pages describe "Washington's corrupt politicians" and career politicians engaged in "near-criminal degrees of waste and self-dealing".

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Said any two people, "regardless of the color of their skin or gender or orientation", should be free to marry.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said no one should be discriminated against and voted for marriage equality and anti-discrimination in marriage regardless of race or orientation.

separated-powers.rationale: Better Government page praises the Founders' checks and balances and separation of powers as what carried the country through challenges.

party-controls-media.rationale: Called the TikTok ban "the same drum as other communist countries controlling what content we are able to see" and opposes governments pressuring platforms to silence dissent.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Demanded the federal funding freeze of a library over sexually explicit books accessible to children and has called for LGBTQ-themed books to be removed.

death-penalty.rationale: Introduced bills to restore the death penalty in D.C. (including terrorism and child abuse) and to authorise it for child rape, and called for it in the Lindsay Clancy case.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Proposed an amendment making citizenship at birth depend on at least one parent being a citizen, national or lawful permanent resident.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Introduced a bill requiring four generations of toxicity data before pesticide approval and a farm-bill amendment to keep states' and localities' power to regulate pesticides.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Voted for the No Rogue Rulings Act saying unelected judges should not override the American people, but elsewhere defends constitutional limits on government.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Introduced the No DEI in DC Act and a resolution ending race-based caucuses, calling them "segregation"; Wikipedia reports she opposed the 2021 COVID-19 Hate Crimes Act partly over discrimination in higher education.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Her Constitution page calls the Constitution the bedrock of liberty and lists religion, speech, privacy, due process and the Second Amendment as rights government must respect.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Her animal rights page calls animal welfare a cornerstone and targets cruel and painful experiments on animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Seeks to prohibit painful research on dogs and cats and opposes mink fur farming but does not oppose animal use generally.

native-born-offices.rationale: Introduced a constitutional amendment requiring members of Congress, federal judges and Senate-confirmed officers to be natural-born citizens.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Posted that every Muslim holding public office is a "trojan horse" and a security threat, later denying she meant anyone Muslim; contested.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Pesticide data transparency is nearby; no stated position on a general legal right of access.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Her 7 October statement calls the attack the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust, treating it as established history.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Bills to bar trans women from women's facilities, to let people sue over gender-transition treatment received as minors, and to keep people diagnosed with gender dysphoria from sensitive federal posts.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Her 2026 bill targets belief in Sharia replacing U.S. law and she said "Total Islamaphobe here" in a post; she also told CNN she was not calling all Muslims a threat.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Voted Yea on the Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act (2022) and has pushed to expose congressional harassment settlements.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Wrote that the U.S. should have the strongest national defense in the world and champions defence-authorisation provisions for the armed forces.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Voted against the Democratic policing bill she characterised as a defund-the-police effort and says she works with law enforcement.

term-limits.rationale: Backs congressional term limits on her Better Government page and signed a term-limits pledge in 2013.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voted Yea on bills (2023, 2024, 2025) barring non-citizens from voting in D.C. elections and repealing its local resident voting law, and says only citizens should vote.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Describes guns as tools for hunting and self-defense, holds a concealed-weapons permit and voted to protect gun owners.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Wrote that sex is binary, male or female, and not a social construct, and the bill codifies reproductive-system definitions of sex.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Her Better Government page backs a balanced budget amendment as a legal limit on federal borrowing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The same bill makes refusing to learn English grounds for denial, and in 2013 she wrote that those seeking citizenship should embrace the culture by speaking English.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Said she believes in "every employee's right to not join a labor union or pay union dues" when voting against the PRO Act (2021).

voter-id.rationale: Voted for the SAVE America Act requiring proof of citizenship and photo ID and sought to move the ID date up to 2026.

no-business-privileges.rationale: In 2013 she opposed picking winners and losers and called for ending crony capitalism; in the 2026 debate she said businesses must pay their own way and incentives should wait until job goals are met.

notes:
Living person: answers come only from her own statements, bills and recorded votes. Views changed: she voted for the Respect for Marriage Act and introduced the States Reform Act (2021) but in 2025-26 made sharply critical statements about gay couples and has campaigned on a more restrictive agenda; the most recent clear positions are used. She lost the 9 June 2026 Republican gubernatorial primary (Wikipedia). Her 2001 book In the Company of Men could not be opened in full text (only excerpts via OnTheIssues). Statements in debate captions were attributed only where moderators named her.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Positions have shifted: on same-sex marriage (voted for the Respect for Marriage Act in 2022, later posted 'Adam and Eve, not Adam and Steve'), transgender policy (from 'strongly support LGBTQ rights' in 2021 to the 2024-25 bills on sex-based facilities and minors' treatment), abortion exceptions, and Trump (critical after Jan 6, later an ally). The most recent clear position is used. Search budget ran out before police, welfare, energy, tariffs and other topics could be checked; those are null, not negative.
